maxRps.rationale: No explicit gateway limit stated; set slightly above normal traffic to reflect an admission ceiling that isn't the bottleneck.

instances.rationale: Prose states 15 instances of the search service.

concurrencyPerInstance.rationale: No concurrency figure given; assume a typical thread/worker pool size for a JVM/Node-style search service handling I/O-bound calls to Elasticsearch.

serviceTimeMs.rationale: No explicit CPU time given for parsing/ranking; assume a modest value typical of query parsing plus result ranking excluding the Elasticsearch call itself.

hitRate.rationale: Prose says hit rates are much lower than typical because search queries are diverse; assume a low hit rate reflecting long-tail query diversity.

hitLatencyMs.rationale: No latency stated; typical round-trip for a remote in-memory cache used in front of a search cluster.

cpuTimeMs.rationale: Typical in-memory cache server processing time per operation, orders of magnitude below round-trip latency.

ttlSeconds.rationale: Prose states search results are cached for 30 seconds.

keyspaceHotSet.rationale: Diverse, long-tail search queries imply a large distinct key space rather than a small hot set, consistent with the low hit rate described.

connectionPoolSize.rationale: Prose states a client-side connection pool of 50 connections to Elasticsearch.

queryTimeMs.rationale: No explicit query time given; assume a typical full-text search query latency for Elasticsearch under normal load.

writeRatio.rationale: Prose states indexing happens on a completely separate pipeline that doesn't touch this read path, so this path is effectively all reads.

readReplicas.rationale: Prose explicitly states no Elasticsearch replicas are run for search traffic.

replicaApplyRate.rationale: No replicas exist for this read path, so replica apply rate is zero.
